almighty.title: Almighty
almighty.note: It translates El Shaddai, a Hebrew title for God used most in the stories of the patriarchs and in Job. It describes who God is and what he can do, and it is not anyone's name.

buzi.title: Buzi
buzi.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
buzi.note: Ezekiel's father. The book opens with Ezekiel the priest, the son of Buzi, and says nothing more about him.

chaldeans.title: Chaldeans
chaldeans.note: They started as one tribal group in southern Mesopotamia and ended up ruling the whole Babylonian empire. In the Old Testament the name came to mean Babylonians in general.

chebar.title: Chebar
chebar.note: A river or canal in Babylonia. Jewish exiles like Ezekiel were settled near it after Jerusalem fell. By the Chebar Ezekiel saw his first vision of God's glory and the living creatures.

diblath.title: Diblath
diblath.note: Ezekiel's judgment runs from the wilderness to Diblah, meaning the whole length of the land. It is most likely a copyist's form of Riblah on the Orontes in Syria, the Babylonian headquarters where Zedekiah was blinded after watching his sons killed.

ezekiel.title: Ezekiel
ezekiel.about: Prophet living at the time of Exile and Return
ezekiel.note: A priest taken to Babylon with the first exiles. Five years in, he saw God's throne, wheels within wheels and four living creatures, and started prophesying. He acted out a lot of it, lying on his side for over a year. His valley of dry bones coming back to life is the picture of Israel restored.

god.title: God
god.note: The Bible never argues that he exists; it assumes it, and Psalm 14:1 calls the man who denies it a fool. The Hebrew is El, from a word meaning strong, or Eloah, far more often in the plural Elohim. Jehovah, the other name, is printed LORD in small capitals in the Authorized Version.

israel.title: Israel
israel.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
israel.note: God gave Jacob this name after he wrestled through the night at Peniel. It became the name of the nation that came from his twelve sons, and later of the northern kingdom and of the land. For the man himself, see Jacob.

jaazaniah-3.title: Jaazaniah
jaazaniah-3.about: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
jaazaniah-3.note: Ezekiel names him once, and he is a man from the exile and the return.

jehoiachin.title: Jehoiachin
jehoiachin.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
jehoiachin.note: Three months on Judah's throne, then he surrendered to Nebuchadnezzar and went to Babylon with much of Jerusalem's upper class. He spent thirty-seven years a prisoner. A new Babylonian king let him out and fed him at the royal table for the rest of his life, and 2 Kings ends there.

jerusalem.title: Jerusalem
jerusalem.note: David took it from the Jebusites and made it his capital, and once Solomon's temple stood there it was the centre of Israel's worship for a thousand years. Babylon destroyed it, the exiles rebuilt it, Rome destroyed it again in AD 70. Jesus died and rose just outside its walls, and Revelation ends with a new Jerusalem coming down from heaven.

judah.title: Judah
judah.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
judah.note: Leah's fourth son, and the brother who ends up leading. He talked the others into selling Joseph rather than killing him, and later offered himself as a hostage in Benjamin's place. His tribe produced David's royal line and gave its name to the southern kingdom, and Jacob's dying blessing promised the sceptre would not leave him.

tammuz.title: Tammuz
tammuz.about: A male deity in the Old Testament
tammuz.note: In Ezekiel's vision the women sit at the temple's north gate weeping for Tammuz. He was the Mesopotamian god of shepherds and growing things, Dumuzi to the Sumerians, and the weeping mourned his yearly death.

tel-abib.title: Tel-abib
tel-abib.note: Ezekiel lived here among the exiles by the river Chebar. The name meant an old ruin-mound in Akkadian, and the founders of Tel Aviv borrowed it in 1910.
